query_text: Why do men have larger Adam's apples?

messages.content: Why do men have larger Adam's apples?

message.content:
Men usually have larger **Adam’s apples** because **testosterone** during puberty makes the **larynx (voice box)** and its surrounding **thyroid cartilage** grow more, so the cartilage sticks out more in the front of the neck.[2][4][6][9]

A few key points:

- **Everyone has an Adam’s apple**; in many people it just isn’t very visible.[2][6][9]
- During puberty, **male larynges typically grow larger**, which also contributes to a **deeper voice**.[4][6][9]
- The **angle and shape of the thyroid cartilage** also affect how prominent it looks, so there is natural variation among individuals.[2]
- Some women and some people who are thin or have higher testosterone levels can also have a noticeable Adam’s apple.[1][2][4]

So the short answer is: **men tend to have larger Adam’s apples because their larynx and thyroid cartilage usually grow more under testosterone influence at puberty**.[2][4][6]
